name: A 1v1 Says When The Opponent Stops Answering
note: D37 (two phones, 2026-10-27 and 2026-10-30): an opponent off the network for 90 s changed nothing on either screen. The gate drives the real battleService on a fake clock with a stub channel; Gemini G2-2 (arming) and M3-2 (stopping) are the two places it was easy to get wrong.

mutations.name: progress arms the watch
mutations.why: Opponents on 31/32 send progress and no heartbeat: thinking over a move for 12 s they would read as gone (Gemini G2-2).

mutations.name: the first beat waits a tick
mutations.why: Until the first beat arrives the other side does not watch at all.
mutations.find: tick(); // the first beat at once
mutations.replace: // tick(); // the first beat at once
mutations.expectFailure: the first beat must go out at once

mutations.name: progress does not stand in for a beat
mutations.why: Twice the writes for the same news.
mutations.expectFailure: a beat went out a second after progress

mutations.name: the tick does not stop itself when the match ends
mutations.why: A finished board stops nothing of its own: the timer would run in the result screen and the lobby (Gemini M3-2).
mutations.expectFailure: the board finished: the timer was left running

mutations.name: stopping leaves the connection watch on
mutations.why: A watch per match, never let go.

mutations.name: a rematch does not start the heartbeat again
mutations.why: The second match would have no heartbeat and no watch.

mutations.name: a lost connection is not shown
mutations.why: The side that dropped off did not know it (2026-10-30).

mutations.name: the opponent is shown as gone later than 12 s
mutations.why: The number the user saw in the 10-29 plan (Diary 167).
mutations.expectFailure: not shown as gone after 12 s

mutations.name: nothing the opponent sends counts as heard
mutations.why: Without it no heartbeat ever arms the watch.
mutations.expectFailure: an opponent silent for 13 s is not shown as not answering
